jobs.description_text: About the Program The Human Frontier Collective (HFC) brings researchers and scientists together to tackle consequential problems in AI. In partnership with the Preparedness and Policy research team , we are building a small cohort of researchers to work on the empirical foundations of AI safety. The work includes thinking about various failure modes, evaluating whether safety controls hold up under pressure in realistic settings, and studying how AI agents (mis-)behave over long-horizon tasks. Residents take open research questions like these and turn them into work that improves how frontier AI systems are evaluated and safeguarded. Research Areas Mentors will guide AI safety residents on projects in AI safety research areas, such as: AI control and chain-of-thought monitoring: Developing techniques to oversee and constrain AI systems, including monitoring their reasoning to detect harmful intent or deception. Alignment red-teaming: Developing science around testing whether models have hidden goals, misaligned behaviors or unsafe tendencies. Multi-agent safety: Studying the risks that emerge when multiple agents interact, such as collusion, coordinated failures, or unexpected collective behavior. Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) safety: Investigating how to keep AI systems safe and aligned as AIs increasingly contribute to their own development. The models feed directly into our wider automated sales operating model, so sellers everywhere present customers with the same credible, defensible numbers. These models will underpin the proposals used across the entire sales organisation, and form the core of the business cases that go in front of customers. They will cover a wide range of deal sizes, products and industries, so they need to be consistent, robust and adaptable. The role has three parts: Identify the value. Understand how each product creates measurable value for customers, across cost efficiency, growth or protection, sustainability and risk reduction. Build the model. Convert that value into a repeatable, standardised financial model, including cash flow, P&L and return metrics, that works across accounts and deal sizes. Tell the financial story. Translate the model and its outputs into a clear, compelling financial narrative that increases the impact of every proposal with customers, including their CFOs and finance teams.
